subtitle: When the Tide Brought Silver and Horses

panels.shot: sweeping wide of a bustling medieval port with ships at anchor and a crowded bazaar in foreground
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat stands on a wooden jetty beside bales of cotton and jars of indigo, gazing over a forest of masts on the Khambhat shoreline as camel caravans and sailors move behind him.

dialogue.text: Long before the sultans came, Khambhat’s Jain merchants quietly ruled a different empire—of cotton, coins and horses—binding Patan to the Arabian Sea.

i18n.hi: सुल्तानों से बहुत पहले, खंभात के जैन बनियों ने चुपचाप एक और साम्राज्य चलाया – सूत, सिक्कों और घोड़ों का, जो पाटण को अरब सागर से बांधता था।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of shoreline at dawn, boats silhouetted against the light, mist over the water
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat stands knee-deep in the tidal shallows, robes hitched, feeling the pull of the retreating tide as small boats sit tilted in the mud around him.

dialogue.text: Here the sea itself is strange. The Gulf of Khambhat empties and fills like a giant lung, its wild tides both a blessing and a risk for every ship.

i18n.hi: यहाँ खुद समंदर निराला है। खंभात की खाड़ी दैत्य फेफड़े सी भरती-खाली होती है, उसके उफनते ज्वार हर जहाज़ के लिए वरदान भी, खतरा भी।

panels.shot: overhead bird’s-eye of Khambhat town and anchorage, showing tidal flats, warehouses and caravans converging
panels.action: From above, the town of Khambhat stretches inland from the muddy creek, with warehouses, Jain temples and caravan-sheds; a caravan of pack bullocks approaches while small craft wait in the channel.

dialogue.text: By the tenth century, Arab travellers wrote of this muddy creek as one of India’s richest ports, a place where caravans met ships and the tide carried fortunes.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी तक अरब मुसाफिर इस कीचड़ भरी खाड़ी को भारत के अमीर बंदरों में गिनते, जहाँ कारवां जहाज़ों से मिलते, और ज्वार किस्मतें बहा ले जाता।

panels.shot: crowded bazaar mid-shot, focus on hands exchanging goods
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat sits cross-legged in a shaded verandah, weighing a bale of fine cotton while another trader displays strings of polished carnelian beads and jars of deep blue indigo.

dialogue.text: Khambhat’s wealth grew from simple things made with great skill—soft cotton, deep indigo, gleaming carnelian beads, all drawn from Gujarat’s soil and hands.

i18n.hi: खंभात की दौलत सादे मगर हुनरमंद हुनर से फूली – मुलायम कपास, गहरी नील, दमकती माणिक्या माला, सब गुजरात की मिट्टी और हाथों से निकले।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a caravanserai where foreign merchants rest and negotiate
panels.action: Inside a long hall, Merchant of Khambhat negotiates calmly with a robed Arab horse dealer and a bearded Persian trader, ledgers open, while grooms restrain restless horses in the courtyard beyond.

dialogue.text: In return came silver and gold, dates and glass—and from across the sea, warhorses that the Solanki kings prized more than any jewel.

i18n.hi: बदले में आती चाँदी-सोना, खजूर, शीशा – और उस पार से जंगी घोड़े, जिन्हें चालुक्य राजे हर जवाहर से ज़्यादा मानते।

panels.shot: interior court scene, three-quarter view, with a king on a low throne and a merchant standing before him
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat stands in respectful posture before a Solanki king seated on a low throne in Patan, court nobles watching as a scribe notes down a grant.

dialogue.text: Behind these exchanges stood the Solanki court at Patan. The king needed bullion and horses; the merchants needed roads, peace and law. Each leaned on the other.

i18n.hi: इन सौदों के पीछे पाटण का चालुक्य दरबार खड़ा था। राजा को चाहिए थे घोड़े और धात, बनियों को रास्ते, अमन और कानून। दोनों एक-दूसरे सहारे टिके।

panels.shot: closer shot on merchant and king, slightly low angle on the merchant to suggest rising influence
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat raises his eyes to meet the king’s, holding a rolled account book; a faint smile touches the ruler’s face as courtiers whisper among themselves.

dialogue.text: Some merchants rose higher still, becoming shreshthins—city elders—and nagarasheths, who spoke for guilds and streets, then for the king’s treasury itself.

i18n.hi: कुछ बनिये और ऊँचे उठे – बने श्रेष्ठी, नगर-श्रेठ, जो पहले पाड़ा और पंच, फिर राजा की कोश तक की ज़ुबान बन गए।

panels.shot: wide of Patan city with temples and markets, linking court and commerce
panels.action: A panoramic view shows Patan’s fortified walls, crowded bazaars and rising temple spires, with Merchant of Khambhat walking between a merchant guild hall and a palace gate.

dialogue.text: In Patan, these Jain shreshthins became a bridge—between street and court, warehouse and war-room, coin and crown.

i18n.hi: पाटण में यही जैन श्रेष्ठी बने पुल – गली और दरबार के बीच, गोदाम और युद्ध सभा के बीच, सिक्के और ताज के बीच।

panels.shot: temple courtyard wide, with inscription stone prominently placed
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat stands in the sunlit courtyard of the Bhadreshwar Jain temple, hand resting gently on a freshly carved stone slab set into the wall.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions at places like Bhadreshwar record their names. Traders of Khambhat and Kutch endow shrines and feeding houses, writing their presence into stone.

i18n.hi: भद्रेश्वर जैसे स्थानों के शिलालेख उनके नाम गाते हैं। खंभात और कच्छ के सौदागर देहर और भोजनशालाएँ दान में देते, अपना नाम पत्थर पर उकेरते।

panels.shot: medium shot of merchant overseeing construction, with artisans at work
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat oversees masons laying dressed stone, carpenters raising beams and sculptors carving Jain images, while villagers watch from under a tree.

dialogue.text: Their profits did not end in warehouses. Jain merchant-ministers like Vimal Shah, and later Vastupal and Tejpal, poured trade wealth into temples, wells and rest-houses.

i18n.hi: उनकी कमाई गोदामों में नहीं थमती। विमल शाह जैसे जैन मंत्री-बनिये, बाद में वास्तुपाल-तेजपाल, व्यापार की दौलत मंदिरों, कुओं, धर्मशालाओं में उड़ेल देते।

panels.shot: interior of a Jain temple hall, serene, with patrons and monks
panels.action: Inside a cool pillared hall, Merchant of Khambhat stands beside a Jain monk, while families sit in orderly rows receiving food from temple volunteers.

dialogue.text: Charity, merit and credit intertwined. Gifts fed monks and the poor—and declared to every trader who entered, who had built this house of stone and trust.

i18n.hi: दान, पुण्य और साख आपस में घुल गए। भोग से साधु और ग़रीब तृप्त, और हर व्यापारी को बताता – यह पत्थर और भरोसे का घर किसने खड़ा किया।

panels.shot: close-up of a hand pouring coins onto a cloth, coins clearly old-style but not labeled
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat tips a small cloth purse onto a low table, spilling thick, irregular coins bearing worn symbols as a young clerk watches closely.

dialogue.text: In their hands clinked new forms of money. Solanki-era gadhiya paisa and other coins moved through bazaars and caravans, oiling the long journey from field to ship.

i18n.hi: उनकी मुट्ठियों में झनकती नई मुद्रा। चालुक्य काल की गढ़िया पैसा और और सिक्के, खेत से जहाज़ तक के सफर को चिकना करते बाज़ारों और कारवां में घूमते।

panels.shot: scholarly, almost documentary overhead of scales and coins, ledgers nearby
panels.action: On a low bench, scales balance as coins are weighed against small metal weights, while a ledger, ink pot and reed pen lie open beside Merchant of Khambhat.

dialogue.text: Numismatists still debate each type and ruler. Yet the pattern is clear: a busy circulation of coin, measure and trust that knit Gujarat’s markets together.

i18n.hi: सिक्काशास्त्री आज भी हर ढंग और शासक पर बहसते हैं। पर नक्श साफ़ है – सिक्के, नाप और भरोसे का तेज़ घुमाव, जिसने गुजरात के बाज़ारों को एक डोरी में पिरोया।

panels.shot: wide coastal shot showing Khambhat and a more distant Kutch shoreline, hinting at network
panels.action: Merchant of Khambhat stands on a bluff, looking out where the hazy line of another shore suggests Kutch, as small ships move like ants along the horizon.

dialogue.text: From Khambhat’s creek to Bhadreshwar’s shore in Kutch, a chain of ports grew. Each town, each shrine, marked another node in this merchant-made state.

i18n.hi: खंभात की खाड़ी से कच्छ के भद्रेश्वर तट तक बंदरगाहों की कड़ी उगी। हर नगर, हर देहर, इस व्यापारी-गढ़े राज्य की नई गाँठ बनती गई।

panels.shot: night-time port wide, with stars, ships and a quiet, reflective mood
panels.action: At night, Merchant of Khambhat stands on the quiet jetty, stars bright above, as anchored ships rock gently and distant temple lamps flicker inland.

dialogue.speaker: merchants_of_khambhat
dialogue.text: A strong wall holds a city. A kept word holds a world.

i18n.hi: किला शहर को बाँधे, निभाया हुआ वचन दुनिया को।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composite wide, hinting at centuries passing with changing ships and clothes
panels.action: In a symbolic scene, Merchant of Khambhat’s figure is echoed by later traders in slightly different dress, while ships of changing designs crowd the same tidal creek over centuries.

dialogue.text: Later travellers like Ibn Battuta and Marco Polo still found Gujarat’s ports busy. Power shifted, dynasties fell, but the merchant routes remembered their old paths.

i18n.hi: इब्न बतूता, मार्को पोलो जैसे बाद के मुसाफिर भी गुजरात के बंदरगाहों को खचाखच पाते। ताकत बदली, वंश गिरे, पर व्यापारी राहें अपने पुराने नक्शे याद रखती रहीं।

panels.shot: final reflective close-up on merchant’s weathered face, sea and temple blurred behind
panels.action: Close on Merchant of Khambhat’s calm, weathered face, eyes catching both the glint of the sea and the outline of a Jain temple rising behind him.

dialogue.text: In the Solanki age, it was not only spears that shaped Gujarat. Quiet Jain merchants of Khambhat proved that trade, promise and coin could bind a kingdom as tightly as any army.

i18n.hi: चालुक्य ज़माने में गुजरात को सिर्फ भालों ने नहीं गढ़ा। खंभात के खामोश जैन बनियों ने दिखाया – सौदा, वादा और सिक्का भी राज्य को सेना जितना मज़बूत बाँध सकता है।

title_i18n.en: Cambay's Ships and the Merchant State
title_i18n.hi: खंभात के जहाज़ और व्यापारी राज्य

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Tide Brought Silver and Horses
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब ज्वार लाता था चाँदी और घोड़े
